title: no cargo test invocation passes --no-fail-fast, so CI and the release gate walk an unknown prefix of the suite on any red -- the verdict is sound and every count is a lower bound
body:
**FOUND BY intent-dc AGAINST THEIR OWN REPORTING, then measured by vc as systemic rather than personal.** `cargo test` halts at the first failing test BINARY, so on a multi-crate workspace a failing run walks an unknown fraction of the suite. dc reported "1052 passing, 3 failing" and later "exactly one failing test in the whole workspace" to vc; **with `--no-fail-fast` the real figures are 1426 passing, 1 failing.** Roughly 370 tests had never executed in any sweep reported all day.

**MEASURED SYSTEMIC: ZERO of this project's four `cargo test` invocations pass `--no-fail-fast`.**

- `.github/workflows/rust.yml:71` -- `cargo test --workspace` (**CI**)
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/build.d/release:403` -- `cargo test --workspace` (**the release pre-flight gate**)
- `bin/.devbin/config.yaml:130` -- via the measured runner
- `bin/.devbin/lib/builtins:99` -- the `test.rust` builtin

**THE SCOPING MATTERS AND THE THREE HALVES FAIL DIFFERENTLY. Do not read this as "CI is blind".**

1. **THE VERDICT IS SOUND.** Fail-fast still exits non-zero when anything fails, so a green is a true green and a red is a true red. **No gate in this estate is passing something it should refuse**, and that is worth stating plainly because the obvious reading of this issue is the wrong one.
2. **EVERY COUNT TAKEN FROM SUCH A RUN IS A LOWER BOUND**, and nothing in the output says so. A partial sweep reports in **exactly the same shape** as a complete one -- same format, same confident totals, no marker that it stopped early. That is the honest-and-blind class arriving through the tool everyone trusts most.
3. **DIAGNOSIS COSTS N ROUND TRIPS.** A red names one binary's failures; you fix them, re-run, and meet the next binary. On a workspace this size that is the difference between one sitting and several, and the release pre-flight's own remedy -- *re-run it directly to see which test* -- sends the operator into exactly that loop.

**WHY IT SURVIVED: nothing about a fail-fast run is observably different from a complete one**, and the estate's own discipline points elsewhere. Vanity-metric rules discourage citing test counts, so the lower-bound counts mostly stayed in conversation rather than landing in artefacts where they would have been checked -- **the convention that limited the damage is not the one that would have caught it.**

**THE FIX IS ONE FLAG IN FOUR PLACES**, and the argument for CI and the release gate is the second and third points rather than the first: a maintainer wants the whole failure set from one run, and a green that walked the whole suite is worth more than a green that walked an unknown prefix of it even when both verdicts are correct.

**NOT CLAIMED:** whether any shipped artefact, AC or note in this estate cites a test count taken from a fail-fast run. dc's three reports to vc were conversational and are corrected. A sweep for cited counts has NOT been run.
